title: Soil Microbiome & Carbon Sequestration
keywords_for_the_page_and_card: Soil biogeochemistry · Root exudates · Fungal networks · Boreal carbon
intro: Boreal and alpine soils hold more carbon per square metre than any other terrestrial system. We ask what keeps it there — and what makes it leave.

Soil core archives spanning two latitudes
add_paragraph:
Fresh plant carbon enters the soil through roots and litter. Whether it stays there depends on a chemistry we are only beginning to resolve: how strongly organic molecules bind to mineral surfaces, how fungal networks redistribute them, and how disturbance changes the rules.

Our field sites run from beech forest in southern Sweden to alpine heath above the tree line. We pair long-term labelling experiments with soil cores measured for carbon chemistry and microbial community structure.
